allow_large: Owner chose this change (2026-10-09): new fields on review, CI-wait and lane records, a per-item time breakdown and round lines in forge board --json, and a How it went section in the pull request, across the recorders, a new records module, the board view and close
done_when: Forge records, in its existing event and timing logs (no new files), each review result's finding titles, severities and files, why each CI wait ended (passed, failed, or gave up while queued or running), and when an item joins and leaves a lane; one place outside board.py works out, per task and fix, where its time went (building, its own tests, reviewing, fixing findings, waiting for CI, waiting in line, waiting for the owner, nothing running) and one plain line per round (what the round did, how long each step took, and how many findings were new versus repeats of an earlier round's); forge board --json carries both per item, and its total no longer counts a worker's test runs twice or leaves out idle time; the pull request body gains a short 'How it went' section from the same data that survives the squash merge; the coordinator guide says how to read and quote them; unrecorded values show as unknown, never invented; command tests cover a looping item with a CI give-up, a lane wait, an owner wait and a repeat finding, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: The substitution searches the entire PR body instead of Forge's managed block. If the owner adds a handwritten `## How it went` section before `<!-- forge:begin -->`, this replaces that section and can consume Forge's opening marker and review summary before reaching the generated heading. The subsequent `pr edit` permanently publishes the damaged body and squashes it. Restrict the replacement to the managed block, preserving everything outside its markers.
findings.title: Preserve handwritten sections when refreshing merge history

findings.body: Every uncovered interval becomes `nothing_running`, although legacy logs do not establish that nothing was running or that the item was not waiting for its owner. New evidence beyond the legacy-history ruling: the earlier-release recorder in `tests/fixtures/forge-v1.2.2/src/forge/repo.py:120` writes timings without round or activity events. With old timings covering seconds 0–10 and 20–25, followed by new activity at second 60, this calculation invents 45 seconds of idle time. The prefix protection at lines 65–67 does not cover gaps between existing legacy records. Preserve those unobserved intervals as unknown until complete activity recording begins.
findings.title: Not done: keep gaps in legacy timing history unknown

findings.body: When earlier findings are unknown, one unseen finding makes `comparable` false for the entire report, erasing known repeat counts too. New evidence beyond the repeat-count ruling: after a recorded finding A, a later report containing A and an unseen B produces `repeat_findings: null`, despite A being an observed repeat. The named legacy test repeats only A, so it misses this mixed-report case. Retain the observed repeat count independently while leaving unseen findings' classification unknown, as the ruling and shipped guide require.
findings.title: Not done: retain observed repeats in mixed legacy reports

findings.body: The looping cases execute `--resolve accept` but only assert that owner time is non-null; they never verify that the review-loop wait stops accruing. Removing `src/forge/close.py:102` would leave these assertions green while the resolved wait remains open. The worker-question test exercises a different producer, and the narrow/split command cases in `tests/test_close_holds_after_three_blocked_reviews.py:89–105` do not check time history. Add a command-level assertion that a review-loop resolution closes the corresponding wait and freezes its recorded duration.
findings.title: Not done: test that resolving a review loop ends its owner wait

findings.body: The review clock starts in `close.py:193`, before admission to the review agent lane in `review.py:541`. The interval calculation correctly separates that queue time, but this special case replaces the calculated reviewing duration with the full timing. A 60-second lane wait followed by a 5-second review therefore shows reviewing 5 seconds in the breakdown, but review 65 seconds plus in-line 60 seconds in the round line and PR. Use the separated reviewing duration so the two presentations agree.
findings.title: Subtract the review lane wait from the round's review duration

why: When a task or fix loops through review rounds, CI waits and queues, nobody can see where its time went: the board and pane show only the current round, the latest findings and a total that double-counts a worker's tests and leaves out idle time; earlier rounds' findings are overwritten, CI giving up is recorded the same as red tests, lane waits and waits for the owner are invisible, and after the squash merge only bare 'Review of X: blocked' lines remain (owner request 2026-10-09, after a review of real long-running items)
